item_name: High-Risk Drug Classes: Use and Indication — Anticoagulant (e.g., warfarin, heparin, or low-molecular weight heparin)

lookback_source.quote: N0415E1. Anticoagulant (e.g., warfarin, heparin, or low-molecular weight heparin): Check if an anticoagulant medication was taken by the resident at any time during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

lookback_notes: 7-day look-back period ending on the ARD; if the resident's admission/entry or reentry occurred less than 7 days before the ARD, the period is "since admission/entry or reentry." The item table on p. N-4 states the window as "during the last 7 days or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days." The item's own pages alternately use the terms "7-day look-back period" (N0415E1, p. N-7) and "7-day observation period" (general coding instruction, p. N-6) for the same window. Counting convention (ARD + 6 previous calendar days) comes from the manual's general conventions, not from this item's pages.

coding_levels.label: Anticoagulant — Column 1: Is taking
coding_levels.definition: Check if an anticoagulant medication was taken by the resident at any time during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: N0415E1. Anticoagulant (e.g., warfarin, heparin, or low-molecular weight heparin): Check if an anticoagulant medication was taken by the resident at any time during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

coding_levels.label: Anticoagulant — Column 2: Indication noted
coding_levels.definition: Check if there is an indication noted for all anticoagulant medications taken by the resident any time during the observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: N0415E2. Anticoagulant: Check if there is an indication noted for all anticoagulant medications taken by the resident any time during the observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

federal_coding_rules.rule: Check Column 1 (N0415E1) if the resident is taking an anticoagulant by pharmacological classification during the 7-day observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days); Column 2 is checked only if Column 1 is checked and there is an indication noted for all medications in the drug class.

source.quote:
Column 1: Check if the resident is taking any medications by pharmacological classification during the 7-day observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).
o Column 2: If Column 1 is checked, check if there is an indication noted for all medications in the drug class.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Code all high-risk drug class medications according to their pharmacological classification, not how they are being used.

source.quote: Code all high-risk drug class medications according to their pharmacological classification, not how they are being used.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Code medications in N0415 according to the medication's therapeutic category and/or pharmacological classification, not how it is used.

source.quote: Code medications in Item N0415 according to the medication's therapeutic category and/or pharmacological classification, not how it is used.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Medications with more than one therapeutic category and/or pharmacological classification must be coded in all applicable categories/classifications, regardless of how the medication is being used.

source.quote: Medications that have more than one therapeutic category and/or pharmacological classification should be coded in all categories/classifications assigned to the medication, regardless of how it is being used.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Include medications given to the resident by any route in any setting (e.g., at the nursing home, in a hospital emergency room) while a resident of the nursing home.

source.quote: Include any of these medications given to the resident by any route in any setting (e.g., at the nursing home, in a hospital emergency room) while a resident of the nursing home.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Do not code antiplatelet medications such as aspirin/extended release, dipyridamole, or clopidogrel as N0415E, Anticoagulant.

source.quote: Do not code antiplatelet medications such as aspirin/extended release, dipyridamole, or clopidogrel as N0415E, Anticoagulant.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Anticoagulants such as Target Specific Oral Anticoagulants (TSOACs), which may or may not require laboratory monitoring, should be coded in N0415E, Anticoagulant.

source.quote: Anticoagulants such as Target Specific Oral Anticoagulants (TSOACs), which may or may not require laboratory monitoring, should be coded in N0415E, Anticoagulant.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Do not code flushes given to keep an IV access patent in N0415E, Anticoagulant.

source.quote: Do not code flushes to keep an IV access patent in N0415E, Anticoagulant.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Code a medication even if it was given only once during the look-back period.

source.quote: Code a medication even if it was given only once during the look-back period.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Count long-acting medications given every few weeks or monthly only if they are given during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: Count long-acting medications, such as fluphenazine decanoate or haloperidol decanoate, that are given every few weeks or monthly only if they are given during the 7-day lookback period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

federal_coding_rules.rule: For transdermal patches, capture the medication in N0415 only if the transdermal patch was applied to the resident's skin during the observation period.

source.quote: To code N0415, only capture the medication if the transdermal patch was applied to the resident's skin during the observation period.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Combination medications should be coded in all categories/pharmacologic classes that constitute the combination.

source.quote: Combination medications should be coded in all categories/pharmacologic classes that constitute the combination.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Herbal and alternative medicine products are not counted as medications for this item.

source.quote: Therefore, they should not be counted as medications (e.g., melatonin, chamomile, valerian root).

federal_coding_rules.rule: Check N0415Z1, None of the above, if none of the listed medications (including anticoagulants) were taken by the resident at any time during the observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: N0415Z1. None of the above: Check if none of the medications above were taken by the resident at any time during the observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

federal.criterion: Review the resident's medical record for documentation that the medication was received by the resident and for the indication of its use during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: Review the resident's medical record for documentation that any of these medications were received by the resident and for the indication of their use during the 7-day lookback period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

federal.notes: Both receipt of the anticoagulant and its indication must be documented in the medical record.

federal.criterion: Review documentation from other health care settings where the resident may have received these medications while a resident of the nursing home (e.g., valium given in the emergency room).

source.quote: Review documentation from other health care settings where the resident may have received any of these medications while a resident of the nursing home (e.g., valium given in the emergency room).

federal.criterion: An "indication" must be an identified, documented clinical rationale for administering the medication, based upon a physician's (or prescriber's) assessment of the resident's condition and therapeutic goals.

source.quote:
INDICATION
The identified, documented clinical rationale for administering a medication that is based upon a physician's (or prescriber's) assessment of the resident's condition and therapeutic goals.

federal.notes: Definition box governs what satisfies Column 2 (N0415E2).

federal.criterion: Assessors should be able to identify the source(s) used to support coding the pharmacological classification on the MDS 3.0 (e.g., a consistently used facility resource).

source.quote: Facilities may wish to identify a resource that their staff consistently use to identify pharmacological classification as assessors should be able to identify the source(s) used to support coding the MDS 3.0.

federal.notes: Framed as a suggestion ("may wish to") but includes the expectation that assessors can identify the source supporting coding.

federal.criterion: Assessors may consult the manufacturer's package insert or work with the resident's pharmacist to confirm the medication's pharmacological classification.

source.quote: Assessors should consult the manufacturer's package insert, which may contain the medication's pharmacological classification. They can also work with the resident's pharmacist to confirm the medication classification(s) for a resident's medication(s).

federal.criterion: Providers are responsible for coding each medication's pharmacological/therapeutic classification accurately; use of the listed external resources is not required for MDS completion.

source.quote: Providers are responsible for coding each medication's pharmacological/therapeutic classification accurately.

case_mix_relevance.notes: The supplied Section N pages do not tie N0415E to any payment or case-mix classification.

conflicts.topic: Terminology for the N0415E window: "7-day look-back period" vs. "7-day observation period"

positions.claim: N0415E1 states the window as the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: Check if an anticoagulant medication was taken by the resident at any time during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

positions.claim: The general N0415 coding instruction states Column 1 covers the 7-day observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: Column 1: Check if the resident is taking any medications by pharmacological classification during the 7-day observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

conflicts.resolution: Not a substantive difference in length — both describe a 7-day window ending at the ARD; terminology differs only. Recorded for transparency.
